question.problem:
The marginal mass functions of the independent discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ are shown below. Given that the corresponding joint probability mass function is $f(x,y),$ find $f(4,3).$

| | $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{X}(x)$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ | $0.7$ | |  | | $y$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.25$ | $0.6$ | $0.15$ | |
| --- | --- | --- |
question.worked_solution:
Two discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ with joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ are independent if and only if 

$$
f(x,y)={f}_{X}(x)\cdot {f}_{Y}(y)
$$

 

for all possible values $x$ and $y,$ where ${f}_{X}(x)$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ are the marginal probability mass functions for $X$ and $Y,$ respectively.

Therefore, since our discrete random variables are independent, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4,3) & ={f}_{X}(4)\cdot {f}_{Y}(3) \\  & =0.2\cdot 0.15 \\  & =0.03.\end{aligned}
$$
